chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Uqba from Burayd al-Ajli from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The owner of the will has the right to return (revoke/change) in it and make new provisions in his will as long as he is alive.

key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: To return, revoke, or change one's decision
key_terms.يُحْدِثَ: To make new or introduce new provisions

ai.seo_question: Can a person change or revoke their will while they are still alive according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this chain to affirm the principle of *ruju'* (revocability) in wills, a key distinction from the finality of inheritance shares. This ruling underscores the testator's autonomy to adjust bequests for charity or specific beneficiaries while alive, reflecting the flexibility of *wasiyyah* as a voluntary act of disposition rather than a fixed legal transfer.
